definition: Initial subset formulation: retaining human planning and evaluation around delegated implementation.
not_this: An initial reading of planning/review accounts, not a claim that people always judge better or that AI never contributes criteria.
rival_explanations: Established professional quality requirements rather than a new AI effect.
confidence_basis: Four selected reported or generalized accounts; no observed quality effects.

supersession_reason: Criteria generation, reciprocal tasking and the non-AI comparator make a simple human-judgment/AI-execution partition inadequate.
definition: Negotiating checkpoints and criteria: people and AI contribute to plans, evaluations and follow-up tasks, while the practical ability to contest or revise the arrangement remains an empirical question.
not_this: Not a permanent human monopoly on judgment, not continuous human inspection, not accountability equated with effective control, and not a practice unique to AI.

negative_case_response.reason: Expand from retaining human review to a variable distribution of criteria formation, checking and task direction; bound the AI-specific claim.
negative_case_response.discriminating_evidence: Observe actual disagreement, attempted override and its consequences; compare matched non-AI work.

rival_explanations: Conventional delegation and review with a new interface.
Responsibility can persist while intervention becomes ineffective.
conditions: relevant knowledge or access to evaluators
consequences: reported retuning and review opportunities; actual control and downstream quality unverified
confidence_basis: Within-pilot category revision prompted by specific contrary accounts; not independent waves of analysis.

definition: Opening workable possibilities: speakers describe starting or handling work through AI that they previously regarded as difficult, costly or beyond available time.
not_this: Not measured productivity, universal novice access, success of a launched business, or durable independence from expertise.

negative_case_response.reason: Retain as a conditional reported possibility, not a universal net gain: migration failures, interface limits and overload restrict it.
negative_case_response.discriminating_evidence: Follow starting, debugging, recovery, workload and sustained use under matched constraints.

rival_explanations: Prepared demos and selected success stories.
Prior expertise, collaborators, capital or altered task scope.
consequences: reported initiation or progress; durable outcome often unknown
confidence_basis: Reported task-level evidence with explicit failures and unmatched comparisons.

definition: Reconsidering what to pursue: AI-mediated examples or representations of prior work become resources for articulating criteria and reorganizing valued activity.
not_this: Not proof of authentic self-knowledge, preference improvement, business causality, or general freedom to redesign a job.
rival_explanations: Confirmation of an existing preference.
Generic generated language and selective recognition.
Retrospective success narrative.
properties: authority to act on a revised preference
conditions: discretion over one’s work; not established for ordinary employees
consequences: reported reorientation or articulation; downstream validity unverified
confidence_basis: One retrospective role-reorientation account and one rubric-generation account; thin, hypothesis-generating support.

definition: Allocating attention through selective dependence: people decide which decisions to retain, automate, revisit or accept as prompts for their own action.
not_this: Not maximum hands-on control, maximum choice, or an assumption that every worker can freely refuse the arrangement.

negative_case_response.reason: More capable workflows may also expand demands beyond attention; the accounts do not establish whether selective delegation resolves this.
negative_case_response.discriminating_evidence: Compare time saved, new obligations, ability to decline tasks and experienced discretion over repeated work.

rival_explanations: Ordinary task management or product defaults.
Founder control or seniority rather than AI capability.
consequences: reported changes in routing and tool choice; net autonomy unknown
confidence_basis: Accounts of retuning and tool preferences; no subordinate or displaced-worker perspective.

supersession_reason: Failures despite repeated patching and disputes about criteria require separating checkpoints from workable correction.
definition: Making evaluation answerable to the task: forming, contesting and revising criteria and checkpoints with human and AI contributions; the presence of review is distinct from the ability to make a consequential correction.
not_this: Neither human review as a guarantee, nor a human monopoly on criteria; does not establish that a preferred criterion improves outcomes.

negative_case_response.reason: A reviewed output or repeated correction can still fail; task criteria themselves may be inadequate or change.
negative_case_response.discriminating_evidence: Follow a disputed criterion through attempted correction and downstream use.

rival_explanations: Conventional delegation and review with a new interface.
Responsibility can persist while intervention becomes ineffective.
dimensions: review present versus consequential change achieved
consequences: reported revisions of labels or judgments; downstream quality generally unknown
confidence_basis: Contrary cases and within-account sequences across eight new interviews; no independent performance assessment.

definition: Opening and sustaining workable possibilities: initiating work through AI is distinct from maintaining it when repair, production requirements or technical constraints become consequential.
not_this: Not measured productivity, universal novice access, success of a launched business, or durable independence from expertise.

negative_case_response.reason: Retain reported novice success against an expertise prerequisite while adding external capability transitions and shutdown as limits on sustained work.
negative_case_response.discriminating_evidence: Track the same task from initiation through independent use and repeated repair across technical regimes.

rival_explanations: Prepared demos and selected success stories.
Prior expertise, collaborators, capital or altered task scope.
dimensions: local adjustment versus external capability change
reported completion versus independent reliable use
consequences: reported initiation, handoff, restart or shutdown; no population or durability estimate
confidence_basis: Contrasting reported sequences, with unverified vendor success stories retained at a lower claim ceiling.
supersession_reason: Capability transitions and thin novice successes require separating entry from sustained operation.

definition: Allocating attention and setting delegation limits: choosing or being assigned what to automate, inspect, restrict or discontinue under expanding demands; choice and workload remain separate empirical dimensions.
not_this: Not maximum hands-on control, maximum choice, or an assumption that every worker can freely refuse the arrangement.

negative_case_response.reason: Add restriction and discontinuation as responses and retain the unresolved possibility that saved effort is absorbed by new or imposed demands.
negative_case_response.discriminating_evidence: Observe who sets workload, who can decline, and what follows a refusal.

rival_explanations: Ordinary task management or product defaults.
Founder control or seniority rather than AI capability.
consequences: reported narrowing and selective review; net employee agency unknown
confidence_basis: Experienced-user accounts and managerial interpretations; no primary subordinate refusal trajectory.
supersession_reason: Expert overload and deliberate restriction sharpen the unresolved distribution of attention and discretion.

definition: Mobilizing resources for correction: redirecting stuck work through other expertise, provider relationships, new interfaces, or changes to the agent’s informational environment.
not_this: Not evidence that all users can obtain the same help, that every intervention succeeds, or that any success must retrospectively prove access to repair resources.

negative_case_response.reason: Thin reported direct novice success may not require specialist support; a patched system may still be withdrawn. Resources cannot be inferred merely from success.
negative_case_response.discriminating_evidence: Measure resource access before outcomes, including unsuccessful well-resourced repairs and successful minimally supported users.

rival_explanations: Task complexity and technical maturity alone.
General organizational problem-solving rather than an AI-specific mechanism.
conditions: availability of relevant expertise or capability
authority or means to obtain it
consequences: reported unblocking or restart; durable outcomes usually unknown
confidence_basis: Converging but unmatched reports; actual differential access and sustained causal effects remain untested.

supersession_reason: Favorable unapproved output and provider reform distinguish criteria, authorization, felt control and actual intervention.
definition: Making evaluation answerable to the task: forming and revising criteria and checkpoints across users, specialists and providers, while distinguishing acceptable content from authorized procedure and effective redirection.
not_this: Not a claim that unreviewed output must be bad, that felt control proves effective control, that humans alone originate criteria, or that provider-stated goals are users’ actual interests.

negative_case_response.reason: Acceptable email content coexists with a failed approval expectation; value constraints can impair performance; an interface can target a feeling of control without observed override.
negative_case_response.discriminating_evidence: Trace disagreements and attempted changes, measuring authorization and task consequences separately.

rival_explanations: Conventional delegation and review with a new interface.
Responsibility can persist while intervention becomes ineffective.
conditions: means to act on the resulting judgment
consequences: reported criterion and artifact changes; no general welfare or control effect
confidence_basis: Source-bound contradictory outcomes and provider/user comparisons; downstream effects and counterfactual intervention remain largely unknown.

definition: Reconsidering what to pursue: AI-mediated examples or prototypes become resources for articulating criteria, continuing, narrowing or declining an intended activity.
not_this: Not proof of authentic preference, improved judgment, durable identity change or freedom for all workers; an idea losing appeal in a tool may reflect tool limitations.
rival_explanations: Confirmation of an existing preference.
Generic generated language and selective recognition.
Retrospective success narrative.
consequences: reported early stopping, elaboration or reorientation; desirability unverified
confidence_basis: One identity account plus generalized prototype accounts and a rubric; no bounded prototype-to-abandonment trajectory.
supersession_reason: Prototype-driven stopping extends the thin goals category beyond identity affirmation.

negative_case_response.reason: Include declining an idea, rather than equating more possible projects with greater agency; do not expand evidence for identity change beyond the original thin account.
negative_case_response.discriminating_evidence: Follow stopped ideas through alternate representations, later decisions and outcomes.

definition: Allocating attention and limiting commitments: selectively delegating, collaborating, withholding access or declining availability while deciding which demands to take on; imposed and chosen activity may coexist.
not_this: Not maximum hands-on control, maximum choice, or an assumption that every worker can freely refuse the arrangement.

negative_case_response.reason: Retain senior boundary-setting and personally enjoyable engagement against inevitable depletion or exclusively managerial pressure; ordinary-worker consequences remain unknown.
negative_case_response.discriminating_evidence: Direct demand/refusal histories, time records, costs and outcomes across positions.

rival_explanations: Ordinary task management or product defaults.
Founder control or seniority rather than AI capability.
dimensions: request to refuse versus accepted refusal
consequences: reported help-seeking, limits and subjective strain/enjoyment; no net agency estimate
confidence_basis: Contrary first-person accounts and mediated aggregate sentiment; role confounding remains.
supersession_reason: Reported refusal and personally compelling engagement prevent a uniform overload or imposed-work story.

definition: Mobilizing resources and changing the diagnosis: redirecting stuck work through local contextual changes, other expertise, provider access or infrastructure, while considering whether the original problem formulation should change.
not_this: Not a sufficient or universally necessary cause of success; not proof that help restores production; not defining resources retrospectively from a favorable result.

negative_case_response.reason: Supported service can still be paused; local intervention can improve a test; noncoder success does not establish absence of expertise. Add reframing without claiming observed durable recovery.
negative_case_response.discriminating_evidence: Measure available resources before the attempt, compare matched tasks and inspect durable outcomes after local/external interventions.

rival_explanations: Task complexity and technical maturity alone.
General organizational problem-solving rather than an AI-specific mechanism.
consequences: reported rewrites, test improvement, unblocking, pause or shutdown; downstream resolution often unknown
confidence_basis: Alternative reported pathways with explicit failure and limited outcomes; not a causal design.
supersession_reason: Specialist reframing, local prompt improvement and paused supported service require distinguishing forms and limits of correction.

definition: Opening and sustaining workable possibilities: initiating work through AI is distinct from maintaining it when repair, production requirements or technical constraints become consequential; little manual coding does not imply little relevant expertise.
not_this: Not measured productivity, universal novice access, success without support, absence of domain or AI-workflow expertise, or durable operational independence.

negative_case_response.reason: Lazar’s and Paul’s accounts concern noncoding entry, not a measured novice level across domains or unsupported success; failures and unknown outcomes remain.
negative_case_response.discriminating_evidence: Document prior domain, organizational, technical and AI experience and outside help before comparing novices and experts.

rival_explanations: Prepared demos and selected success stories.
Prior expertise, collaborators, capital or altered task scope.
dimensions: local adjustment versus external capability change
reported completion versus independent reliable use
conditions: time and support for sustained work
consequences: reported initiation, handoff, restart or shutdown; no population or durability estimate
confidence_basis: Audited scope correction to prior terminology; commercially selected reports and incomparable expertise dimensions remain limitations.
supersession_reason: Independent audit requires replacing broad novice labels with explicitly situated noncoder claims.

definition: Turning capacity into commitments: organizational actors use increased contributions, written context and evaluation arrangements to assign work, coordinate others and define what counts as acceptable participation.
not_this: Not a claim that all responsibility is imposed or harmful, that AI caused organizational restructuring, or that leaders’ greater capacity measures workers’ agency.

negative_case_response.reason: Senior refusal and public challenge prevent universal coercion; reorganization provides a non-AI explanation; even leaders report burdens. Direct worker consequences are missing.
negative_case_response.discriminating_evidence: Matched tasks, direct worker/manager accounts and recorded attempts to change assignments or evaluation rules through known endings.

rival_explanations: Rapid growth and conventional hierarchy.
Voluntary role expansion and collective coordination.
Survivor selection and managerial self-presentation.
dimensions: individual benefit versus effects on others
consequences: reported allocation rules, feedback uses and dissent; net employee agency unknown
confidence_basis: Concrete allocation practices plus source-limited organizational narratives; insufficient direct worker outcome evidence.
